claim: Coolify officially supports Debian-based (Debian, Ubuntu - all versions, non-LTS Ubuntu requires manual install), Redhat, SUSE, Arch, Alpine and Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit; other distros may work but are untested, and the docs explicitly recommend a fresh server to avoid conflicts with existing applications.
quote: It's best to use a fresh server for Coolify to avoid any conflicts with existing applications. ... Docker installed via snap is not supported!

claim: Coolify has hardcoded port-80 validation: coolify-proxy fails to (re)start from the web UI with 'Port 80 is in use' even when the proxy is reconfigured to custom ports like 5080/5443, making coexistence with an existing reverse proxy on port 80 a known friction point (repo ~56.6k stars).
quote: Port 80 is in use. You must stop the process using this port.

claim: The official/recommended way to move Coolify's dashboard off the default port 8000 is an upgrade-safe docker-compose.override.yml in /data/coolify/source/ (or setting APP_PORT in .env), keeping the container port at 80; ports 80/443 must remain free for the Caddy/Traefik proxy if using HTTPS custom domains.
quote: create a docker-compose.override.yml file in /data/coolify/source/. This method is 'upgrade-safe' ... Keep the container port at 80 (only change the host port) ... Ports 80 and 443 must remain available if using HTTPS with custom domains.

claim: Docker (and thus Coolify) breaks in an unprivileged Proxmox LXC because runc 1.2+ writes net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0 which the mapped root cannot do without CAP_NET_ADMIN, and the AppArmor profile probe reads host-root-owned /sys paths; the working config is a privileged LXC with features nesting=1,keyctl=1,fuse=1, lxc.apparmor.profile: unconfined and an empty lxc.cap.drop.
quote: runc 1.2+ unconditionally writes to net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0 ... the mapped root lacks the necessary CAP_NET_ADMIN capability ... features: nesting=1,keyctl=1,fuse=1 / lxc.apparmor.profile: unconfined / lxc.cap.drop:

claim: For production Docker workloads on Proxmox the 2026 verdict is to use a KVM VM rather than Docker-in-LXC: VMs give full kernel isolation, live migration and 'standard Docker, no hacks', whereas Docker-in-LXC is 'the worst of both worlds' with fragile workarounds, costing only ~256-512MB extra RAM.
quote: VM + Docker is the production choice ... 'standard Docker, no hacks' ... Docker-in-LXC as combining 'the worst of both worlds' with 'fragile workarounds'

claim: A community guide runs Coolify successfully in a privileged Proxmox LXC with the nesting feature enabled, chosen for being lightweight and easy to migrate around a cluster, with the main friction being networking (single-IP hosts needing Cloudflare tunnels).
quote: uncheck unprivileged container ... go under options to enable the nesting feature flag which will enable nested virtualization ... running coolify in an LXC makes it easy for me to move it around my proxmox cluster, and also its very light weight

claim: Coolify preview deployments are disabled by default; once enabled, every PR opened against the configured branch auto-deploys to a unique URL, and the GitHub App method is recommended because it posts automated status comments on the PR.
quote: Preview deployments are automatically deleted once the associated pull request is merged or closed, ensuring a clean environment.

claim: A real user set up Coolify PR previews by creating a private GitHub App through Coolify (auto-collecting App ID, Installation ID, Client ID/Secret, Webhook Secret) requesting read access to administration/code plus read/write on pull requests for commenting, and a Cloudflare wildcard '*' A record to the server IP.
quote: requested read access to administration and code, plus read/write access to pull requests for commenting on PRs ... creating an "A" record in Cloudflare with hostname "*" pointing to the server IP

claim: Coolify has no upper limit, TTL, or auto-expiration for preview deployments; the 'Max Concurrent Builds' setting only caps build parallelism, so accumulating previews can exhaust RAM/CPU and degrade production on constrained homelab servers (repo at 56.6k stars).
quote: every PR opened against the configured branch creates a preview deployment with no limit ... The existing "Max Concurrent Builds" server setting only limits build parallelism, not running environments ... No TTL or auto-expiration mechanism exists

claim: Coolify isolates preview containers via {uuid}-pr-{id} naming and prioritizes preview-specific env vars when pull_request_id !== 0; GitLab is supported through a parallel webhook controller, but the database isolation strategy is undocumented and lifecycle management is manual.
quote: When a deployment is identified as a preview (pull_request_id !== 0), the system prioritizes or includes preview-specific environment variables ... GitLab is explicitly supported ... database isolation strategy and resource scaling limits are unspecified

claim: For Docker Compose multi-service apps, Coolify rewrites container names per preview (e.g. db-pr-295, frontend-pr-295), which breaks hardcoded service references in nginx upstreams and DB connections; workarounds involve a separate DB instance plus env vars or the COOLIFY_BRANCH variable.
quote: the docker compose file that is generated changes the container names (db-pr-295, frontend-pr-295 etc.). This breaks the connection to the database, and nginx config, as it relies on the original container names.

claim: Versus managed cloud preview platforms, Coolify requires custom configuration for per-preview database provisioning (no automatic database forking) and lacks automated teardown scheduling / idle-detection cleanup.
quote: Coolify and Fly.io require custom configuration for database provisioning in preview environments ... Coolify lacks "automated teardown scheduling"—a feature Northflank includes for idle detection and schedule-based cleanup.

claim: The Coolify repo is coollabsio/coolify, Apache-2.0 licensed, with 56.6k GitHub stars, advertising 280+ one-click services and describing itself as a self-hostable alternative to Heroku/Netlify/Vercel managed via SSH.
quote: Repository: coollabsio/coolify ... Star Count: 56.6k stars ... License: Apache-2.0 ... 280+ one-click services ... open-source & self-hostable alternative to Heroku / Netlify / Vercel

claim: Self-hosted Coolify is free forever with full access to all features and no restrictions; Coolify Cloud is $5/month base (2 servers) plus $3/month per additional server, 20% off annual, where you bring your own servers.
quote: Self-Hosted ... Free Forever ... Full access to all features ... Cloud ... $5/month base price (covers 2 servers) + $3/month per additional server ... 20% discount option for annual ... bring your own servers

claim: Coolify offers four build packs to deploy from git repositories: Nixpacks (auto-detects language and generates a Dockerfile), Static, Dockerfile, and Docker Compose.
quote: Coolify offers Nixpacks, Static, Dockerfile, or Docker Compose build packs to create optimized Docker images ... Nixpacks checks your git repository and generates a Dockerfile ... can only be used on git-based deployments

claim: Coolify v4 reverse proxying runs through Traefik or Caddy from one dashboard with automatic Let's Encrypt SSL provisioning and renewal; v4 introduced multi-server support letting you add remote servers via SSH and deploy to any from the same dashboard.
quote: Reverse proxying runs through Traefik or Caddy ... Coolify automatically provisions and renews Let's Encrypt SSL certificates ... V4 introduced proper multi-server support ... add remote servers via SSH and deploy applications to any of them from the same dashboard

claim: Coolify v4.0.0 shipped April 27, 2026 after about two years in beta; as of March 2026 the project had over 52,200 GitHub stars and a reported 325,000+ users.
quote: Coolify v4.0.0 shipped on April 27, 2026 after about two years in beta. As of March 2026, Coolify has over 52,200 GitHub stars and a reported 325,000+ users

claim: Coolify itself consumes roughly 1GB of RAM before any apps are deployed, so the 2GB minimum leaves almost no headroom; 4GB is a realistic production minimum and 4 vCPU/8GB/100GB NVMe is the comfortable sweet spot for multi-app use.
quote: Coolify itself eats about 1 GB of RAM before you deploy anything, so the 2 GB minimum leaves almost no headroom ... 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM / 100 GB NVMe is the comfortable sweet spot

claim: Coolify v4 is built on a Laravel/PHP stack run via Docker Compose with services including Postgres, Redis, and Soketi (WebSocket server on ports 6001-6002 in dev) for real-time status events.
quote: Soketi WebSocket server provides real-time updates with status change events for applications, services, databases, and proxies, running on ports 6001-6002 in development

claim: Coolify supports standalone one-click database instances including Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, Clickhouse, KeyDB, and Dragonfly, and integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Gitea for git-based deploys.
quote: Coolify supports standalone database instances including Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, Clickhouse, KeyDB, and Dragonfly

claim: In January 2026 Coolify disclosed 11 critical vulnerabilities (CVSS up to 10.0) enabling auth bypass, RCE and root access, with ~52,000 instances exposed.
quote: Coolify, a popular self-hosted deployment platform, disclosed 11 critical vulnerabilities (CVSS up to 10.0) enabling authentication bypass, remote code execution, and root access, exposing over 52,000 instances worldwide to potential takeovers.

claim: CVE-2025-64419 (CVSS 9.7) allows arbitrary command execution with elevated privileges; CVE-2025-64420 (9.9) exposes a private SSH key to low-privileged users; CVE-2025-64424 (9.4) lets low-priv members run arbitrary commands; ~52,650 hosts exposed, disclosed Jan 5 2026.
quote: CVE-2025-64419 (CVSS 9.7) ... execute arbitrary system commands with elevated privileges ... CVE-2025-64420 (CVSS 9.9) ... low-privileged users to access a private SSH key ... 52,650 exposed hosts ... the trivial nature of the exploit make active exploitation highly likely

claim: An August 2025 bug deletes manually-added Docker volumes (permanent data loss) when a Dockerfile service is stopped/redeployed, because the 'Delete Unused Volumes' cleanup setting is enabled by default (coolify repo ~56.6k stars).
quote: Volumes get delete when stopping a service if `Delete Unused Volumes` is activated ... It looks like the issue is something similar to this older issue that was marked as completed #5343 but applies to Dockerfile services.

claim: A user broke Coolify by clicking the web-UI update button repeatedly (it isn't disabled after click), running the update script multiple times and losing their Laravel APP_KEY, rendering old projects unrecoverable with 'The MAC is invalid'.
quote: the button doesn't get disabled. It seems like the update script starts running multiple times when you click it again ... the encryption key ... Error: The MAC is invalid ... This will be fixed in the next version.

claim: In beta.434 Coolify generated malformed Traefik routing labels (empty Host matcher, domain mis-placed in PathPrefix) causing 502 Bad Gateway and SSL failures, persisting across beta.418-434 and requiring manual config after every deploy.
quote: This bug makes Coolify unusable for production deployments without manual intervention after every deployment.

claim: Coolify's default Traefik v3.1 proxy fails against Docker Engine 29.x with a Docker API version mismatch, returning 503 for all hosted apps until fixed in beta.444 (Traefik v3.6).
quote: the default traefik:v3.1 proxy fails to communicate with Docker, resulting in 503 errors ... client version 1.24 is too old. Minimum supported API version is 1.44

claim: HN commenters reported Coolify had so many Docker-deployment bugs they couldn't trust it in production, plus a long-standing unfixed issue of random CPU spikes to 100%.
quote: I experienced so many bugs around docker deployments I just couldn't trust it for production ... There's also a long standing issue of random peaks to 100% CPU, that they don't seem to be able to fix.

claim: A 2025 production comparison found Coolify's flow required too many clicks, that stopping/starting an app triggered a full rebuild from scratch, and that the author preferred Dokploy for getting out of the way in production.
quote: Coolify's flow required too many clicks for me ... stopping and starting the app triggered a rebuild from scratch ... Coolify layers its own platform logic on top of Compose

claim: Coolify ran in production at thousands of companies while formally remaining in beta the entire time, with the maintainer admitting 'it has many' bugs that are fixed daily.
quote: thousands of companies have been running Coolify in production for one to two years already - formally, however, in beta the entire time ... This does not mean it has no bugs, it has many, but we fix them every day.

claim: Coolify offers native per-branch deploy support with isolated environments at unique subdomains; Dokku needs a plugin and manual config for multi-env, while Kamal and CapRover lack native preview functionality; install times on Debian/Ubuntu are ~30 min (Coolify, curl+UI), ~20 min (Dokku CLI), ~20 min (CapRover docker run), ~15 min (Kamal YAML); Kamal is a deploy tool not a PaaS with no server abstraction.

claim: Komodo is a self-hosted fleet/container management platform (Rust backend, Periphery agents) with build pipelines from Git and compose-stack deployment across servers — positioned as a Portainer alternative with built-in CI/CD, not a Vercel-style PR-preview PaaS.
quote: Komodo is built for fleet management with a Rust backend, Periphery agents, build pipelines from Git ... can be thought of as a Portainer alternative with built-in CI/CD capabilities

claim: Coolify's own backup covers the instance/dashboard settings (Postgres DB restored via pg_restore, SSH keys at /data/coolify/ssh/keys, APP_KEY in /data/coolify/source/.env) but NOT application data/volume mounts, which must be backed up manually.
quote: This only backs up and restores the Coolify instance itself — not your application data. ... application data (such as volume mounts) must be backed up and restored manually.

claim: Coolify supports S3-compatible storage destinations (Amazon S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi) and runs scheduled pg_dump/mysqldump/mongodump on a cron schedule, storing locally and optionally pushing to S3.
quote: Coolify supports S3-compatible storage for backups, including Amazon S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, and Wasabi.

claim: Coolify offers three upgrade modes—automatic (checks CDN and self-updates), semi-automatic (UI 'Upgrade' button on notification), and manual via 'curl -fsSL https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/install.sh | bash'; docs warn to always back up before upgrading.
quote: Always back up your Coolify data before starting an upgrade ... curl -fsSL https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/install.sh | bash

claim: Coolify v4 sends notifications to Email (SMTP/Resend), Telegram, Discord, Slack/Mattermost, Pushover, and generic Webhook, with per-channel event routing for deployment success/failure, backup success/failure, scheduled tasks, disk usage, and server reachable/unreachable.
quote: Coolify supports these channels: Email, Telegram, Discord, Slack / Mattermost, Pushover (Push Notifications), and Webhook ... You can configure different events for each notification channel

claim: Coolify v4 is a complete ground-up rewrite (announced April 2, 2023) moving from v3's SvelteKit/Node.js stack to Laravel/PHP, motivated by developer experience and making the project 'more professional - it is not a side-project anymore.'
quote: a complete rewrite from scratch ... more professional - it is not a side-project anymore. ... The DX is not the best. The frameworks are limited and only do one or a few things well.

claim: Coolify Cloud is a managed option at $5/month (includes up to two connected servers) plus $3/month per additional server, where the Coolify team handles all upgrades; the self-hosted version stays fully free.
quote: Coolify Cloud users don't need to manage upgrades—the team handles all updates
